name: The Later Han Empire, with the first Buddhist houses
blurb: Rome's exact contemporary and ahead of it in metallurgy, agriculture and bureaucracy. Cast iron for five centuries already, the seed drill, the moldboard plough, paper in the year 105, water-powered blast bellows in 31 AD. This variant adds the first Buddhist houses as a landholding and lending body. Needs `mod-allow bh_religion_h5p1` for the house to exist.

cast.actors.name: the Buddhist houses and their patrons
cast.actors.source: Hou Hanshu ch.42 (Liu Ying, King of Chu, 65 AD, favours the Buddhist rites) and the tradition of the White Horse Temple at Luoyang, 68 AD; Zurcher, The Buddhist Conquest of China (1959), ch.1: no monastic estate, mill or pawnshop is attested before the fourth to fifth centuries, so the start-date house is a few hundred people on a few hundred hectares and no mill. Later monastic mills and pawnshops (the 'inexhaustible treasuries'): Gernet, Buddhism in Chinese Society (1995), ch.3-4. The sizes are placeholders of the right order, not counts.
cast.actors._heuristic: land_share_of_surplus is the share of a year's surplus the house spends on land and land_ceiling_hectares the most it will hold (three times its start, a guess); a stand-in until donors, the house's own rule and the land market's offers are modelled actors (Complaints/636).
